guideTitle: 6 Best Large-Display Calculators With Big Buttons in 2026
metaDescription: Six large-display, big-button calculators compared by screen size, digit count, function keys and power source so numbers stay easy to read at a glance.
introParagraphs: Reading a result should never feel like a vision test. A large display with high-contrast digits lets you glance at the answer and move on, and big keys mean you press what you meant to press. Together they remove most of the small frustrations of everyday arithmetic.

The calculators here all pair a sizeable screen with oversized keys, but they stretch the idea in different directions. One offers a 4.2 inch readout, two push to five inches, and some add grand total or memory keys for people who track running figures.

We ranked them from the listed specs and recurring buyer feedback themes, not from lab readings. Where a listing leaves out a detail such as key material or tilt, we say so and suggest what to confirm before you order.

products.name: CATIGA Premium Commercial 12-Digit Calculator
products.description:
This commercial-grade CATIGA pairs a five-inch twelve-digit screen with giant responsive buttons. The maker says the clear display relieves eye strain, which matters if you check numbers for long stretches.

It also carries grand total, markup and memory clear, recall, add and subtract keys. Those tools handle both simple sums and more involved totals without a second device. The trade-off is that a feature-rich panel has more keys to learn than a bare four-function unit.

Compared with the Podokas, it offers a larger readout and richer function keys. Against the M&G, it focuses on screen size and function depth rather than a raised key shape. It is the pick that best combines a big display with big keys and useful extras.
products.bestFor: People who want the largest screen plus grand total, markup and memory keys.
pros: Five-inch twelve-digit screen is the biggest in this group
Grand total key keeps running sums in one place
Giant responsive buttons are easy to hit accurately
Memory add, subtract, recall and clear are all included
cons: More function keys take longer to learn
Larger body needs a clear stretch of desk

products.name: pendancy Extra Large 5-Inch Accounting Calculator
products.description:
The pendancy tilts a five-inch screen to 30 degrees so the digits face your eyes rather than the ceiling. Orange, blue and gray keys on a silver panel help you tell function groups apart quickly.

The giant response buttons and ABS plastic body are built to be light but sturdy. The listing frames it as an accounting model, so it includes the functions that role needs. Battery and solar details are sparse on the page, so verify them before buying.

Compared with the CATIGA Premium, it shows a similar screen with fewer named function keys. Next to the yxzzhx, it leans on colour coding instead of a stated ergonomic tilt. Choose it if you like to find keys by colour as well as position.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a five-inch tilted screen and colour-coded keys for quick scanning.
pros: Colour-coded keys let you find functions by sight
30 degree tilt points the digits toward your eyes
ABS body stays light while resisting knocks
Giant response buttons are easy to press
cons: Listing gives little power source information
Colour mix may feel busy to some users

products.name: yxzzhx Desktop Calculator with 5-Inch Display
products.description:
The yxzzhx stresses an ergonomic screen tilt that reduces neck strain, with a five-inch twelve-digit display. The listing says it aligns with your natural line of sight when it rests on a flat desk.

Two-way power lets it run in sunlight or on the two AA cells that ship with it, so you can use it straight away. The listing says less about key material and special functions than the CATIGA Premium does, which keeps the feel basic.

It works well for someone who simply wants numbers big and the neck relaxed. Compared with the pendancy, it is clearer about power and what comes in the box. Choose it for comfort during long sessions.
products.bestFor: People who spend long stretches at the desk and want a comfortable viewing angle.
pros: Ergonomic tilt reduces neck strain on a flat desk
Two AA cells are included for immediate use
Five-inch display shows twelve digits clearly
Solar assist works in good light
cons: Few details on function keys or key material
No named memory or grand total features

products.name: Podokas Large 12-Digit Dual Power Calculator
products.description:
The Podokas lists a 4.2 inch extra-large LCD that shows up to twelve digits. Its buttons are described as larger than usual, which suits use at home, school or in an office.

Two-way power lets you carry on in a bright spot if the cell runs out. The listing mentions many rounds of key testing, though it does not give a number we can quote. It keeps the feature list basic, so there are no grand total or markup keys to confuse you.

It makes sense for a household that wants a simple, big-screen unit. Compared with the CATIGA Premium, the screen is a little smaller and the function list is shorter. Choose it when you prefer simplicity to a busy panel.
products.bestFor: People who want a big screen and big buttons without extra business functions.
pros: 4.2 inch LCD is big enough for easy reading at a glance
Buttons are larger than on a standard calculator
Dual power adds a safety net when a cell runs low
Simple feature set avoids clutter
cons: Smaller screen than the five-inch models here
No grand total or memory keys listed

products.name: M&G Large LCD Desk Calculator
products.description:
The M&G shows twelve digits on a large LCD and builds its keys with a recessed, raised shape. That shape is meant to make your input flow and keep presses accurate.

It uses solar or an AAA cell, and one AAA battery arrives in the box. The sturdy plastic keys are described as durable. The listing does not state a screen size in inches, so you need to compare it against the others by look rather than a number.

It is a neat fit for someone who types numbers quickly and wants well-defined key tops. Compared with the Podokas, it focuses on key shape rather than a stated display size. Choose it when the feel of the keys is your top priority.
products.bestFor: Quick typists who want well-defined, raised key tops and an included battery.
pros: Raised recessed key tops guide your fingertips accurately
AAA battery arrives in the box
Sturdy plastic keys are described as long lasting
Twelve-digit LCD handles longer totals
cons: Screen size is not stated in inches
No named grand total or memory keys

products.name: HIHUHEN Multi-Functional Big Button Calculator
products.description:
The HIHUHEN uses a Japanese LCD for a twelve-digit display and adds big buttons. It handles negative numbers, percent and square root, and lets you set rounding and decimal places.

Memory keys MC, MR, M+ and M- come as standard, and CE/C separates a partial clear from a full one. That level of control helps with budgeting where you want exact decimals. It runs on solar or one AA battery, with a cell included.

Compared with the Podokas, it offers deeper functions but no stated screen size. Against the CATIGA Premium, it lacks a grand total key but adds rounding control. Choose it when precision settings matter to you.
products.bestFor: Budget keepers who want rounding, decimal control and a full memory set.
pros: Rounding and decimal place setting for exact answers
Four memory keys plus separate CE and C clear
Square root and percent keys add flexibility
Battery included alongside solar power
cons: Screen size is not given in inches
No grand total key like the CATIGA Premium

buyingCriteria.explanation: Words like large mean little without a number. Look for inches and compare them. The CATIGA Premium and pendancy list five inches, the yxzzhx lists five inches, and the Podokas lists 4.2 inches. Prefer a stated size over vague wording.

More digits show longer totals without cutting numbers off. Eight is typical, twelve gives headroom. Every pick here lists twelve digits, so the difference is in screen size and key layout. Check that the digits themselves are tall, not just numerous.

Large keys prevent slips, and a raised or recessed shape guides your finger. The M&G lists recessed big buttons, while the CATIGA Premium lists giant responsive buttons. Choose a shape that matches how firmly you press.

Extra keys help only if you use them. Grand total, markup and memory suit bookkeeping, while basic users want fewer. The CATIGA Premium has all three, and the Podokas keeps to basics. Match keys to your tasks.

A tilted screen faces your eyes and cuts overhead glare. A 30 degree tilt is common. The pendancy lists a 30 degree view, and the yxzzhx lists an ergonomic tilt. Prefer a tilt if you sit close to the desk.
Solar saves cells, but a backup keeps the screen alive in dim light. The yxzzhx ships with two AA cells, and the M&G ships with one AAA. Prefer a model that arrives ready to use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Screen size and clarity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated display sizes and digit counts. The CATIGA Premium, pendancy and yxzzhx list five inches, the Podokas lists 4.2 inches. We could not verify contrast, so we relied on specs and buyer feedback.

howWeEvaluated.title: Key size and shape
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how keys are described, such as giant, recessed or raised. The M&G and CATIGA Premium stand out for different reasons. Scores favour designs that reduce mis-presses.

howWeEvaluated.title: Function usefulness
howWeEvaluated.description: We judged which extra keys help everyday users. The CATIGA Premium offers grand total and markup, while the HIHUHEN offers rounding control. Keys that most buyers never use earned less credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Viewing comfort
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted tilt and angle claims. The pendancy lists 30 degrees and the yxzzhx lists an ergonomic tilt. Listings without a tilt were scored more cautiously.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The CATIGA Premium leads on function depth, the pendancy on colour coding, the yxzzhx on viewing comfort, the Podokas on simplicity, the M&G on key shape, and the HIHUHEN on rounding control.

faq.a: The CATIGA Premium, pendancy and yxzzhx each list a five-inch screen. The Podokas lists 4.2 inches. The M&G and HIHUHEN do not state a size in inches.
Twelve digits gives headroom for large totals. All six picks list twelve. If you only handle small sums, the size of the digits matters more than their count.

faq.q: What is a grand total key?
faq.a: It adds up several results into a single running total. The CATIGA Premium includes one along with markup and memory. It suits bookkeeping more than casual use.
They face your eyes and reduce glare. The pendancy lists a 30 degree view and the yxzzhx lists an ergonomic tilt. Flat-lying models may suit you less if you sit close.
Yes. The yxzzhx ships with two AA cells, the M&G with one AAA, and the HIHUHEN with a battery. Check the box listing for the others.

faq.q: How do I clean the display?
faq.a: Use a soft dry cloth and avoid sprays. Moisture can seep around the keys. Keep it out of direct sun when storing to prevent warping.
